facts.heading: Anxiety worsening since September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and it has gotten worse since September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time, and it's got worse since September.

facts.heading: Became deputy head
facts.content: Hannah was made deputy head at her school. She has taught Year 4 for eleven years.
facts.evidence: I was made deputy head at my school. I've taught Year 4 for eleven years

facts.heading: Fear of being judged
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she has no idea what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Thoughts occur Sunday evenings
facts.content: Hannah's anxious thoughts happen mostly on Sunday evenings.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings. My chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Rehearsing staff meeting
facts.content: Hannah rehearses what she might say for the staff meeting.
facts.evidence: I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Imagining negative thoughts
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth. That they gave the job to a nice Year 4 teacher who can't actually lead.

facts.heading: Rewrote email four times
facts.content: Hannah rewrote an email to the governors four times last week.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of seeming stupid
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr Hargreaves would think she was stupid regarding the email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr Hargreaves, the chair of governors, would think I was stupid.

facts.heading: Mr Hargreaves' reaction
facts.content: Mr Hargreaves told Hannah he was delighted in September.
facts.evidence: He told me in September he was delighted.

facts.heading: Feeling like a liar
facts.content: Hannah feels she is lying to Mr Hargreaves about her capabilities.
facts.evidence: That makes it worse somehow, because I feel I'm lying to him.

facts.heading: Pretending to be capable
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is pretending to be someone who knows what she is doing.
facts.evidence: About being capable. As if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Comparing to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares her work to her mother's career.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's career
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for twenty years.
facts.evidence: She was a headteacher for twenty years.

facts.heading: Mother's legacy
facts.content: People in the village still praise Hannah's mother's work.
facts.evidence: Everyone in the village still stops me to say what a wonderful head she was.

facts.heading: Mother's retirement
facts.content: Hannah's mother retired six years ago.
facts.evidence: She retired six years ago and they've named a library after her.

facts.heading: Mother's support
facts.content: Hannah's mother says Hannah has always worried too much.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Feeling like a fuss
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss when her mother offers support.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel I'm making a fuss.

facts.heading: Waking up at four AM
facts.content: Hannah is awake at four every morning going through a to-do list.
facts.evidence: That I'm awake at four every morning. I fall asleep fine, then I'm awake at four going through the to-do list.

facts.heading: Waking due to work stress
facts.content: Hannah has been waking up at four since the second week of term. She drinks a lot of coffee to cope.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term. I drink a lot of coffee to get through the day, which I know doesn't help.

facts.heading: Physical symptoms during afternoons
facts.content: Hannah experiences a fast heart rate and shaky hands in the afternoons.
facts.evidence: My heart goes fast. My hands are a bit shaky.

facts.heading: Hiding physical symptoms
facts.content: Hannah had to leave a meeting to splash her face with water. She feels exhausted from pretending.
facts.evidence: Last Thursday I had to leave a meeting to splash my face with water. I'm exhausted by the end of every day just from pretending.

facts.heading: Partner's advice on feelings
facts.content: Ben suggested Hannah should enjoy her situation. Hannah feels guilty and alone when he says this.
facts.evidence: He says I should just enjoy it. Guilty, and a bit alone.

facts.heading: Partner's profession and view
facts.content: Ben is an engineer and believes problems can be fixed. Hannah feels this is not the case.
facts.evidence: He's an engineer, he thinks if something's a problem you fix it. And you can't just fix this.

facts.heading: Loss of school friendships
facts.content: Hannah has lost friends she used to see in the Year 4 corridor. She misses them.
facts.evidence: Now I'm their line manager and it's awkward. I miss them. I miss my class too.

facts.heading: Missing children's experiences
facts.content: Hannah misses the daily moments when a child receives something for the first time. Her days are now spreadsheets.
facts.evidence: The children, honestly. The daily bit where a child gets something for the first time. Now my days are spreadsheets.

facts.heading: Desire for promotion
facts.content: Hannah thought she wanted the promotion and said yes because she couldn't say no to the head.
facts.evidence: I thought I did. I said yes in the room because I couldn't say no to her. the head.

facts.heading: Tears about the promotion
facts.content: Hannah cried after saying yes to the promotion. The tears were about fear and never getting to go back.
facts.evidence: Fear, I think. And that I'd never get to go back.

facts.heading: Last time feeling relaxed
facts.content: Hannah felt properly relaxed during the summer holidays. She did not think about school for ten days.
facts.evidence: The summer holidays. We went walking in the Lakes, and I didn't think about school once for ten days.

facts.heading: Pre-term distress
facts.content: The week before term, Hannah was a wreck again. She could not eat on Sunday.
facts.evidence: The week before term I was a wreck again. I couldn't eat on the Sunday.

facts.heading: Tried writing down good things
facts.content: Hannah started writing down what went well each evening. This helped for about two weeks.
facts.evidence: I started writing down what went well each evening. Small things. A child laughing, a good email. It helped for about two weeks

facts.heading: Stopped writing things down
facts.content: Hannah stopped writing things down because she felt silly.
facts.evidence: and then I stopped, because I felt silly. As if I were bragging to myself in a notebook. Noticing what went well is not the same as bragging.

facts.heading: Wants to do job without fraud
facts.content: Hannah wants to do her job without feeling like a fraud.
facts.evidence: I'd like to do the job without feeling like a fraud.

facts.heading: Goal for Tuesday at work
facts.content: Hannah wants to walk into a meeting without rehearsing it first and sending only one email.
facts.evidence: Walking into a meeting and not rehearsing it first. Sending an email once.

facts.heading: Goal for Sunday evening
facts.content: Hannah wants to be able to sit on the sofa in the evening without her stomach being in knots.
facts.evidence: Being able to sit on the sofa in the evening without my stomach in knots.

facts.heading: Feels lighter after sharing
facts.content: Hannah felt lighter and a bit tearful after stating her goals out loud.
facts.evidence: Lighter. A bit tearful, actually.

facts.heading: Has not told Ben about issue
facts.content: Hannah has not told anyone how bad things are, not even Ben.
facts.evidence: That it's the first time I've told anyone how bad it is. Not even Ben knows about the four a.m.

facts.heading: Worried about telling Ben
facts.content: Hannah thinks telling Ben would be scary and he might be hurt.
facts.evidence: Scary. He'd probably be hurt that I didn't say sooner.

facts.heading: Wants quiet moment to tell Ben
facts.content: Hannah thinks choosing a quiet moment would help her tell Ben.
facts.evidence: If I choose a quiet moment. Not on a Sunday evening, then I'm too wound up.

facts.heading: Suggests Saturday morning for Ben
facts.content: Hannah suggests Saturday morning over breakfast as a time to tell Ben.
facts.evidence: Saturday morning, perhaps? Yes, over breakfast. He's always in a good mood then.

facts.heading: Agrees to try notebook again
facts.content: Hannah agreed to try the evening notebook again for a week.
facts.evidence: I could. I'll put it by the kettle so I don't forget.

facts.heading: Nearly cancelled session this morning
facts.content: Hannah nearly cancelled the session this morning but was glad she did not.
facts.evidence: Only that I nearly cancelled this morning. I'm glad I didn't.
